newsitem.title: USA: MCI unit blames U S West unit for delay.
newsitem.headline: MCI unit blames U S West unit for delay.

text.p: MCI Communication Corp's local telephone service unit has postponed its entry into the Colorado market and blamed U S West Communications Group for its difficulties.

MCI's MCImetro unit said it has asked the Colorado Public Utilities Commission to delay its scheduled start date of July 31. It said U S West Communications, a unit of U S West Inc and the regional Bell operator in Colorado, supplied it with a substandard ordering system.
U S West Communications responded that its system works fine and is serving other local phone companies in other markets.
The MCImetro accusation reflects a pattern of complaints from companies encountering problems entering the local phone service markets dominated by the regional Bell companies.

MCImetro said U S West Communication's ordering system makes it difficult or even impossible for MCImetro to enlist residential phone service subscribers, the company said. The ordering system executes the switch of customers from the Baby Bells to new local competitors.
"U S West's system doesn't work and certainly cannot support the volume of customer transactions that MCI expects to generate," MCI regional director Bill Levis said.
U S West Communications said its Internet-based ordering system is providing services to at least two other local competitors in the 14 local phone markets it serves.

A U S West Communications spokesman dismissed MCImetro's complaints as a smokescreen to mask the long distance carrier's in-house problems orchestrating a move into Colorado's local phone service market.

"What is really at issue here is that MCI is not prepared to get into residential service in this part of the country, and they're looking to blame someone for that shortcoming," U S West Communicatinos spokesman David Beigie said.
Beigie said MCI wants a system tailor made to its demands, but MCImetro has not cooperated with U S West Commnications in the development of that system.
MCImetro said the Colorado commission will be briefed by staff on the matter at its June 25 meeting.
